How to bake bread

by J. Writer4 March 2026

Bread is mostly patience. You mix flour, water, salt and a little yeast, and then you wait while something slow and biological happens to it. Every recipe you will ever read describes the same four ingredients, and none of them can describe the part that matters, which is knowing when to stop waiting.

What you need

  • 500 g strong white flour
  • 350 g water at room temperature
  • 10 g salt
  • 3 g dried yeast

The proportions are a starting point and not a rule. Flour absorbs water differently depending on how it was milled and how long it has been sitting in your cupboard, so the dough you get on a damp week will not be the dough you got last month.

The method

Mix the flour and water first and leave them alone for half an hour before adding anything else. This does most of the kneading for you, which is the single best trick in the whole process and the one most recipes leave out.

Shaping

Shape it with as little flour on the bench as you can manage. Extra flour on the outside of the loaf turns into a dry seam once it bakes.

Patience is an ingredient, and it is the only one you cannot buy.

Bake at 250C with steam for twenty minutes, then drop the heat and let it finish. The loaf will keep cooking after you take it out, so pulling it slightly early is the safer mistake.
